heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: SpaceX's first earnings after the June IPO beat ($12.7B consensus) as AI ('Super Intelligence') hit $7.56B, now ~52% of revenue, and Starlink connectivity grew 69% to $5.25B; but Q3 capex was $19.6B and Q4 is guided to $35–40B, mostly AI, so it is increasingly not a pure space story. Starship Flight 15 (first attempted ship catch plus booster pad catch) is now listed for Nov 13, 22:45 UTC, pending regulatory approval, per Space Launch Schedule (Nov 7); earlier NET Nov 8 has passed.

kpis.sub: SPCX OCT 30 CLOSE · PRICE NOT REFRESHED THIS RUN · ~40% BELOW $225.64 JUNE HIGH
kpis.label: No fresh SPCX quote was captured this week, so the Oct 30 close of $134.72 is the last reliable figure; the sector sold off again on Nov 5. Merger committees at SpaceX and Tesla are still studying a combination (no terms found); the next big supply event is ~797.6M shares around Dec 8 (third-party schedule, verify against the prospectus).

kpis.sub: RKLB LATE-WEEK QUOTE (UNDATED TICKER) · Q3 REPORT TODAY NOV 9 AFTER CLOSE
kpis.label: Results land after the close today, so they are not in this refresh. Q3 guidance is revenue $250–265M (vs $155M a year ago), adjusted EBITDA loss $17–23M, non-GAAP gross margin 35–37% (41.5% in Q2); Neutron's first flight is 2027, and the $8B Iridium deal (approved by IRDM holders Sept 24) is guided to close mid-2027. A ~$1.94B September stock sale helps fund it.

kpis.sub: Q3 2026 PRIVATE SPACE INVESTMENT · RECORD QUARTER
kpis.label: Seraphim counts 216 deals in Q3 (median $9.8M) versus $7.4B in Q2; Blue Origin's ~$10B round is nearly half the total, so excluding it the quarter is still ~$10.8B. Blue Origin said Oct 16 that Florida infrastructure investment has passed $3B. On Nov 7 NASA's Moon Base awards added a $10B-ceiling CLPS 2 lander pool (eight firms) and a $94M (+ up to $140M option) PROMISE rover award to Blue Origin.

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Reported ~$10B raise at a ~$130B valuation (its first outside round, described as oversubscribed). On Oct 16 it announced a $330M Rocket Park phase at Cape Canaveral with two more New Glenn pads, saying Florida investment has passed $3B; New Glenn returns to flight after the May pad explosion at LC-36 — year-end 2026 per some reports, early 2027 per Blue Origin's own update — with multi-vehicle operations targeted for summer 2027. On Nov 7 NASA awarded it a $94M base (up to $140M more in options) contract to deliver the PROMISE nuclear-powered rover, named it a VADR task-order awardee and a CLPS 2 selectee. Vulcan (ULA) is separately due back Nov 13.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Already public (NASDAQ: FLY), so outside the private groups. Shares $20.76 on Nov 6; Q2 revenue $117.7M (+659%); Q3 results Nov 10 after the close; named a CLPS 2 selectee and VADR in-space transport provider on Nov 7. Not given a stance here for lack of current data.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: No new update this week beyond the earlier $1B Series E (total raised $2.3B); Nova Block 2, a fully reusable design, remains targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: SpaceX spent $19.6B of capex in Q3 and guides $35–40B for Q4, mostly for AI; Rocket Lab (which sold ~$1.94B of stock in September) still guides to a $17–23M Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss while funding an $8B Iridium deal; Blue Origin needed a ~$10B raise. Funding is abundant now, but the sector depends on it staying that way.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: The SDA's Tranche 3 tracking awards ($1.75B across L3Harris and Sierra Space in July) and Redwire's NITE STAR slot (one of 15 vendors, no guaranteed revenue) show how much revenue hangs on a few federal programs. Starshield restrictions in Ukraine show a single operator's decisions can become a geopolitical issue.

bear_case.title: SpaceX dominance and supply overhang
bear_case.description: SPCX closed $134.72 on Oct 30, ~40% below its June high, with ~797.6M lockup shares due around Dec 8 and a possible Tesla merger adding uncertainty; its spectrum purchase and Starlink Mobile put it directly against AST SpaceMobile, and AI is now over half its revenue, so owning it is no longer a clean space exposure.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk and schedule slips
bear_case.description: Neutron's first launch slipped into 2027 (at least the third delay, no new date), AST had a BB7 launch incident and has 13 satellites against a ~45 target, New Glenn is grounded until year-end or early 2027, and Starship's catch and refuelling remain unproven (Flight 15 timing unconfirmed). RKLB fell 23%, ASTS 33% and LUNR 27% in October alone.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Neutron's slip into 2027 and a ~$53 share price (about 23% down in October) hurt sentiment and Q3 gross margin is guided down to 35–37%, but Q2 revenue of $234.1M (+62%), a $2.36B backlog and $250–265M Q3 guidance (reported tonight) keep the Electron-led business intact.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Q3 beat with a record $53.2B backlog, GAAP EPS $3.28 and FY26 EPS guidance raised to $12.25–12.35, though Space & Mission Systems book-to-bill was only 1.0x. Also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure.

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $116.05M (+58%), a fifth straight EPS beat and $13.9M adjusted EBITDA are the best fundamentals among the small caps, but $11.17 after a 12% drop on Nov 5 with Barclays' $17 target shows the market is not paying for it yet.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $206.2M, a $1.76B backlog and a CLPS 2 pool slot (Nov 7) are real, yet equity is about -$290M, a $235M at-the-market raise is diluting holders and the stock fell to $8.47 on Nov 5, so it stays small.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: A Q2 revenue miss ($31.5M vs $34.4M), four straight EPS misses, a $125.9M BB7-related loss and SpaceX's spectrum push outweigh $1.3B of backlog; at roughly $32 (from ~$58 in September) it is cheaper, but Q3 lands tonight and commercial service slipped to early 2027.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Q3 revenue of $109M missed by ~$17M, free cash flow was -$66.4M and the stock fell 21% to $6.13; the record $619.7M backlog and 32.3% gross margin do not offset a full-year guide that now needs a heavy Q4 and shipment-timing risk into 2027.

positions.name: BlackSky
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $33.3M (+50%) with positive adjusted EBITDA of $4.7M is good progress, but a GAAP loss of $0.54 per share and a ~54% drop since April leave the earnings quality unresolved.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Q3 revenue of $14.6B (+161%) and $4.4B net income are strong, but AI is now over half of revenue, Q4 capex is guided to $35–40B, ~797.6M lockup shares are due around Dec 8 and the stock was $134.72 on Oct 30 (not refreshed since), with Tesla merger terms still unknown. UK investors wanting indirect exposure can use Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Q3 EPS of $0.98 vs $0.34 expected was a clean beat, but the deal (~$27 cash plus Rocket Lab stock, ~$54 per share, closing mid-2027) ties it to RKLB's slide — RKLB remains the cleaner way to express the view.
